pages.text: Dad's waterwheel turned. Clunk-a-clunk, clunk-a-clunk. Mumu watched with his chin in his hands.
"I want a waterwheel of my own." Mumu made two little waterwheels from twigs and leaves. They looked like identical twins.
Dodo peered at them. "Waterwheels turn best in a strong current. I know!" Mumu gently handed her one.
Dodo put the little waterwheel in the middle of the stream. Water rushed past.
Whoosh! The current snatched it away. Downstream it floated.
They ran along the bank. "Stop there! Stop!" Dodo shouted.
The little wheel disappeared far below. Dodo scratched her head. "The current... cheated."
Mumu looked at the shallow channel by the yard. The water trickled at just the right speed.
In the channel, the little wheel spun around and around. "It's turning! It's turning!"
Oh, look! The lost waterwheel was caught on Dad's wheel, turning around and around. Dodo called, "Your waterwheel went to work with Dad!" They both giggled.
